rationale: Frozen from three .NET 10 full-pipeline pilot runs, fixed tokenizer fixtures, and a separate .NET 8 Docker load-only smoke. The larger native 500-1000 RSS endpoint rate was 888832 bytes per 100 requests; 2000000 bytes per 100 requests is a 2.25x margin. The target is 3000000000 decimal bytes; reserve 600000000 bytes (20%) as deployment headroom. A separate 64000000-byte late growth cap is 10.7% of that reserve and 14000000 bytes above the slope-only 50000000-byte allowance over 2500 requests. Managed heap uses half that retained-growth cap. Replicate peak/end tolerances are 5%; the 25% slope tolerance is about three times the observed native RSS endpoint-rate difference, with a third replicate required on disagreement. R-squared 0.95 is a strict fit-quality floor and never independently establishes a leak. These are POC acceptance inputs, not measured formal outcomes or a production SLA.
limitations: Native pilot requests used .NET 10.0.12 and ONNX Runtime 1.30.0.0. The Docker smoke used .NET 8.0.31 but executed load-only with zero requests; it is not a matched request replicate. Native repeats ended at 1000 requests, so the 2500-5000 formal late segment and 3000000000-byte Docker target remain untested. Collector/writer/latency-window allocations were not isolated against a telemetry-disabled control. Native host cgroup limits were unavailable at the visible mount; in-container memory.max was available in the load-only smoke. Changed thresholds require a new policy hash, campaign, and rerun of required evidence.
